doc.title: Jane Bunnett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 25, 2024

title: Does Afro-Cuban music swing? Ed Shaughnessy on swing
summary: She says the music is different, full of subdivisions and vibrations; Rowe quotes Ed Shaughnessy's definition of swing.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Does it swing? Does the music swing for you?

It’s different. I mean it can in a way but you can hear that sort of underlying it but there’s always just the, a lot of the time in the music there’s so many subdivisions so rhythmically it’s more so like, it’s vibrations. There’s like just kind of I don’t know sometimes I felt very, very energized from playing the music, that it has given me something back. And it’s a different kind of thing. Yeah.
Swing is hard too, You know I’m still trying to get it together.

Well here’s what drummer Ed Shaughnessy had to say. I asked him what is swing and he went on for quite a while so I’ll just — he says, “Now I think bluegrass music swings like hell. The main thing that swing means for me is it’s infectious, a beat that makes you want to move, it gets you going. So any music like bluegrass or jazz or funk or Watusi music communicates to you rhythmically and gets a visceral thing going. That’s what I think swing is.”
He hit it right on. Yeah.
